newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST - Avmin to lift Anglovaal H1 shr.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Avmin to lift Anglovaal H1 shr.

text.p: South African holding firm Anglovaal Ltd will post strong interim earnings next week as healthy gains in Avmin Ltd are set to outweigh poor earnings from Anglovaal Industries Ltd, analysts said on Friday.
"The results will be pretty good. Avmin is coming through strongly. About half of Anglovaal's earnings are from Avmin. With (Avmin's) earnings up the results will be good.
"Investors will be pleasantly surprised by the results because they would be thinking that weak results from AVI would flow through to Anglovaal," said an analyst who asked not to be identified.
Analysts polled by Reuters forecast earnings per share for the six months to December 1996 ranging between 490.1 to 509.0 cents with consensus at 497.7 cents from 377.0 cents last time.
The dividend was forecast ranging between 61.1 to 63.5 cents with consensus at 62.2 cents, up from 47.0 cents.
Mining group Avmin's interim earnings per share surged to 43.6 cents from 10.9 cents, while industrial group AVI's interim earnings slipped to 72.3 cents from 97.2 cents previously.
Avmin announced recently that it was close to signing an option agreement on the development of Zambia's Konkola North mine.
It also said early on Friday that it was bidding for the bulk of working assets in the privatisation of Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines (ZCCM).

The results are seen giving an indication of the success of a restructuring process implemented at the group last year. "The results will show the measure of change. The (Zambia) copperbelt stuff is all looking good for the company. The results will show what sort of company (Avmin) will be," said one analyst who asked not to be named.
Analysts said that despite its poor performance AVI might have reached bottom and could now start picking up.

An analyst pointed out that Anglovaal's results would depend on the accounting practice they adopt. "If they use the same one as Avmin, then their results will look good. If they do not then they will not be so good," he said.
But other analysts said the accounting practice was immaterial to Anglovaal.
"The accounting practise does not matter. Most of their results are by way of dividends," one said.
